data.title: Mice fed rapamycin have an increase in lifespan associated with major changes in the liver transcriptome
data.authors: Fok WC; Richardson A et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Rapamycin-fed mice show extended lifespan with major changes in the liver transcriptome.
data.abstract_excerpt: Rapamycin was found to increase (11% to 16%) the lifespan of male and female C57BL/6J mice most likely by reducing the increase in the hazard for mortality (i.e., the rate of aging) term in the Gompertz mortality analysis. To identify the pathways that could be responsible for rapamycin's longevity effect, we analyzed the transcriptome of liver from 25-month-old male and female mice fed rapamycin starting at 4 months of age. Few changes (<300 transcripts) were observed in transcriptome of rapamycin-fed males; however, a large number of transcripts (>4,500) changed significantly in females.

extracted_findings.effect: Rapamycin increased lifespan 11-16% with major changes in the liver transcriptome
extracted_findings.dose: 14 ppm encapsulated rapamycin in food, ad libitum, starting at 4 months of age until end of life
extracted_findings.sample_size: 175 mice total (40 control males, 45 Rapa males, 45 control females, 45 Rapa females)
extracted_findings.effect_size: Rapamycin increased lifespan 16% in females and 11% in males (entire survival curve analysis), and significantly increased mean (14% females, 7% males) and maximum (19% females, 8% males) survival.
